$comment: gate-119 (procedure-code), decision 182: procedures are configuration, code is generic.
THE ONE FILE that says what counts. Edit the lists here, not in the checker.
A file COUNTS when its path, or a class/interface/trait/enum it declares, names a Dutch procedure.
substringTokens  matched anywhere in the lowercased path or class name (long tokens that no other word contains).
wordTokens       matched only as a whole word after camelCase/snake/kebab splitting. Short tokens live here,
so 'woo' does not match 'Wood' and 'dso' does not match a word that merely contains it.
A counted file is EXCLUDED when it is a national-standard adapter:
allow.words         whole-word (or hyphenated word run, 'dso-adapter') in the path or class name.
allow.pathPrefixes  repo-relative prefixes, case-insensitive. This is how an ambiguous token such as 'dso' is
excused: by WHERE the file lives, not by the token alone.

allow.pathPrefixes also lists exact files of integriq's DSO-LV adapter (STAM koppelvlak, PKIoverheid signatures, DSO-SWF, status push, DSO exceptions and PKI admin). Exact files, because they are not under one directory. They match case-insensitively in every app, so check another app does not share a path before adding one. The DSO activity-to-zaaktype mapping and samenloop logic is NOT excused: it is procedure logic and stays counted (decision 188).
